answer:
Main analysis executed as approved (statsmodels OrderedModel, proportional-odds cumulative logit; positive coefficient = higher odds of more severe COVID-19).

PRIMARY ESTIMAND — severity conditional on COVID-19 (n=151 cases with recorded AESEV; outcome = subject-level max AESEV 1–4; BCG=1 vs Placebo; covariates: prior medical history count (0–7), patients_seen (1/2/3), treatment×patients_seen interaction):
- BCG vs Placebo OR = 0.79 (95% CI 0.17–3.69, p=0.76) at the reference contact level (1–50 patients seen). Because of the interaction, the BCG OR varies with contact frequency: 0.79 (0.17–3.69) at 1–50; 1.07 (0.52–2.21) at 51–100; 1.46 (0.58–3.72) at >100 patients seen. The interaction term itself is not significant (OR 1.36, 0.48–3.90, p=0.56).
- Other covariates: history count OR 1.25 (0.91–1.71) per additional condition; patients_seen OR 1.05 (0.52–2.11) per level.
- Main-effect-only version (interaction dropped): BCG OR = 1.19 (0.64–2.23).

SECOND ESTIMAND — all 1000 subjects, "no COVID-19 AE" as lowest level (0–4); 43 COVID cases with unrecorded severity assigned the mildest level 1 (all were non-serious events):
- BCG OR = 1.62 (0.73–3.63) at 1–50; 1.19 (0.84–1.69) at 51–100; 0.88 (0.51–1.49) at >100. Interaction OR 0.73 (0.41–1.32). Excluding the 43 instead: OR@1–50 = 1.99 (0.82–4.80); assigning them level 4: 1.48 (0.67–3.29). Main-effect-only: 1.10 (0.80–1.51).

CONCLUSION: In no specification does the 95% CI for the BCG effect exclude 1 — the data provide no evidence that BCG vaccination changes COVID-19 severity (point estimates range ~0.8–2.0 depending on specification and contact level), and no significant treatment×contact-frequency interaction.

PROPORTIONAL-ODDS TEST (executed, as required): violated in both models (Model A LR=29.7, df=8, p=0.0002; Model B LR=34.7, df=12, p=0.0005). Brant-style per-variable tests localize the violation to the prior-history-count covariate (p=2.6e-6 and 0.0013), NOT to treatment (p=0.071 and 0.56), contact frequency (p=0.92/0.79) or the interaction (p=0.31/0.91). A fully non-parallel (category-specific) cumulative-logit fit is unstable due to data separation at the sparse upper cutpoints (only 18 of 151 cases at severity ≥3; e.g., BCG/>100 cells contain no mild cases), so cutpoint-specific ORs are reported only as qualitative sensitivity; the treatment effect shows no consistent departure from proportionality.

SENSITIVITIES: expect_interact replacing patients_seen: BCG OR 2.27 (0.79–6.52) when No vs 0.82 (0.38–1.77) when Yes (interaction p=0.13, ns). Missing-severity bounding (n=194): OR@1–50 = 1.18 (0.30–4.64) if missing=mildest, 0.45 (0.12–1.66) if missing=most severe — wide, non-significant, direction unstable. Including "Other:" free-text MH conditions in the count leaves conclusions unchanged (e.g., OR 0.75, 0.16–3.53 at ps=1). Sparse-cell warnings: several TRT×patients_seen×severity cells have 0–3 observations; Wald CIs are correspondingly wide.
